source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: Through the checkpoint, a traveler's suitcase moved along the conveyor. The queue stretched ahead, where each person, after placing their belongings, walked through the archway of the metal detector, their steps echoing the sterile ambiance, as if each movement were scripted and rehearsed, yet every individual felt the unique tension of personal scrutiny. Belongings lay scattered, items separated, a ritual of divestiture before the machines. A tray held a laptop, phone, and shoes, placed carefully, systematically, under the watchful eyes of the officers. She approached, her documents ready, as an officer motioned for her to step aside. He spoke calmly, his voice measured, asking for her cooperation, explaining the routine check, a simple formality. Three minutes passed, the scanner whirred, the wand traced, and she stood still, understanding the necessity, the controlled environment around her. Her belongings returned, she nodded, thanked him, and continued on her journey, the formalities complete, the process seamless, almost ceremonial. She glanced back, the scene a tableau of efficiency, the impersonal yet polite interactions a hallmark of security. She walked forward, the line steady, the pace relentless, her turn now past, the next traveler stepping up.

The crowd moves slowly, and one officer scans each bag, pausing to inspect suspicious contents, as another directs traffic with gestures. Security screens every bag, ensuring safety. A traveler stands aside, his documents checked meticulously by a vigilant officer. He complies, though visibly tense, under the watchful gaze. Each person follows the rules, guided by clear signs and polite, if distant, officers. Two metal detectors hum quietly, awaiting the next pass. In the bustling hall, an officer wands a selected individual, confirming clearance. They resume their journey, reassured by the routine. She nods, gesturing him through, back into the stream of travelers, efficiently.
